coverage_note: Wyoming has no general public-sector collective bargaining statute in the sources captured. The only bargaining statute found covers paid firefighters of cities, towns and counties (Wyo. Stat. 27-10-101 to 27-10-109); this row records that statute and the right-to-work act.

governing_statute.value: No general statute. Firefighter bargaining under Wyo. Stat. 27-10-101 to 27-10-109
governing_statute.quote: The fire fighters in any city, town or county shall have the right to bargain collectively with their respective cities, towns or counties and to be represented by a bargaining agent in such collective bargaining as to wages, rates of pay, working conditions and all other terms and conditions of employment.

source.title: Wyo. Stat. Title 27, Labor and Employment (title PDF)

labor_board.null_reason: No Wyoming statute captured creates a public-sector labor relations board; the firefighter statute names no administering agency (a district judge picks the third arbitrator if the parties' arbitrators cannot agree, 27-10-106).

ulp_limitation_period.null_reason: No public-sector unfair labor practice procedure was found in the Wyoming statutes captured for this row.

who_may_bargain.value: Paid members of any regularly constituted city, town or county fire department; no statute captured grants bargaining to other public employees
who_may_bargain.quote: (i) The term "fire fighters" shall mean the paid members of any regularly constituted fire department in any city, town or county within the state;

source.title: Wyo. Stat. Title 27, Labor and Employment (title PDF)

scope_of_bargaining.value: Wages, rates of pay, working conditions and all other terms and conditions of employment (firefighters); contracts may not exceed two years
scope_of_bargaining.quote: This obligation shall include the duty to cause any agreement resulting from negotiations to be reduced to a written contract, provided that no such contract shall exceed the term of two (2) years.

impasse_procedure.value: Arbitration of all unresolved issues if no agreement within 30 days of the first meeting, before a three-member board under the Uniform Arbitration Act
impasse_procedure.quote: In the event that the bargaining agent and the corporate authorities are unable, within thirty (30) days from and including the date of their first meeting, to reach an agreement on a contract, any and all unresolved issues shall be submitted to arbitration.

strike_legality.null_reason: No Wyoming statute directly prohibiting or permitting public-employee strikes was found in Title 27 as captured. Not asserted from memory.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. Wyoming's right-to-work act bars requiring dues or fees as a condition of employment, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: No person is required to pay or refrain from paying any dues, fees, or other charges of any kind to any labor organization as a condition of employment or continuation of employment.
